title: Tencent rolls out AI model trained with limited cybersecurity data amid hacking fears
extract: Tencent says its new Hy4 model restricts cybersecurity training to defensive tasks such as finding software flaws and helping patch them, excluding material for building hacking tools or breaking into systems.

title: Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval
extract: Reuters reports roughly 600,000 H200 accelerators are sitting in Hong Kong awaiting approval for mainland shipment, highlighting the tension between China's AI compute demand and reluctance to depend on US chips.

title: India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
extract: India's CERT-In has named the group Crafty Falcon and identified four AI-enabled tools used in attacks on non-bank lenders, fintech firms and crypto exchanges; at least two tools are linked by researchers to China.

title: IBM, AMD, Oak Ridge National Laboratory launch quantum error correction platform
extract: The collaboration pairs IBM's quantum processors with Oak Ridge's AMD-powered Umbra supercomputer so researchers can test hybrid methods for detecting and correcting quantum errors.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber with 'Critical' cybersecurity rating
extract: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to vetted security customers, citing work uncovering Firefox and Linux kernel vulnerabilities and developing patches for critical findings.

title: Anthropic's models improving nearly twice as fast with help from AI, study finds
extract: An independent METR study found Anthropic's benchmark capabilities have been improving about 1.9 times faster since October 2025, as AI tools increasingly help build successor models.

title: Discord is ditching Electron and its new app uses less RAM
extract: Discord is moving its desktop client from Electron to Rust, aiming to cut resource use while sharing more code across desktop and mobile clients.

title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
extract: Perplexity's always-on Teammates can take on separate roles in a workspace, reuse existing projects and memory, and run ongoing tasks through the company's Computer system; the feature requires its $200-per-month Max plan.

title: Muse has a voice mode now
extract: Meta is rolling out real-time voice conversations for its Muse AI agent, with animated avatars and selectable vocal styles; the feature is initially available in the US.

title: 'Conker? Ultimate? Dream? Zelda?' - Rare co-founder Tim Stamper wants to know what fans want him to reveal first
extract: Rare co-founder Tim Stamper is preparing to open his archive on YouTube, inviting fans to choose which material from his four-decade career should be revealed first.

title: 'Next Stop? Production Line!' - Retro Games Ltd offers an update on its recreation of the Atari 800XL
extract: Retro Games Ltd says firmware development for its Atari 800XL recreation is complete and the hardware is entering final manufacturing stages, with shipping still scheduled for April 2027.

title: 'Commodore Is Returning to Shelves Soon' - The C64 Ultimate is headed to physical retail
extract: The revived Commodore has signed an exclusive distribution deal with Colby to bring the C64 Ultimate to physical stores across Europe and parts of Africa and Asia, with US expansion still being worked on.

title: 'Battlespire Rules' - after 29 years, the secret of this Elder Scrolls Easter egg has finally been revealed
extract: A newly donated archive of Elder Scrolls creator Julian LeFay's papers revealed how to trigger a hidden 1997 Battlespire Easter egg: hold the 1 key and type Spire during a game.

title: Speedrunner discovers the formula to Dampé's RNG gravedigging in Zelda: Ocarina of Time
extract: A former speedrunner has decoded the 1998 N64 game's gravedigging RNG by spotting a tell in gravedigger Dampé's blinking pattern, turning a long-standing mystery into a near-reliable method.

title: This impressive new Game Boy Color game may look a little familiar to F-Zero fans
extract: Developer Shane McCafferty has released Zero, a Mode 7-inspired anti-gravity racer for Game Boy Color, adding another technically ambitious homebrew title to the handheld's library.

title: Crazy Taxi meets GTA in Downtown Dash, a new arcade-style racing game for your Atari Jaguar
extract: Dr Ludos has released an open-source 3D arcade racer for Atari Jaguar, built in six months with help from the homebrew community and using community-created tools, sound and models.

title: The wait is over! Taito's 1987 shmup Exzisus joins Arcade Archives today
extract: Taito's 1987 shoot-'em-up Exzisus has arrived in Hamster's Arcade Archives, bringing its robot-mech space combat to modern PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo platforms with additional modes.

title: EA is bringing 25 classic PC games to Steam
extract: EA is bringing 25 classic PC titles to Steam; a rediscovered media vault let the company restore Road Rash and six Wing Commander editions, including more than 1,500 recovered FMV scenes.

title: 'He was destined for this award': China Miéville wins Goldsmiths prize for 1,200-page novel
extract: China Miéville's 1,264-page paranormal thriller and historical saga The Rouse has won the Goldsmiths Prize, praised for its scale, formal experimentation and blend of British imperial and Cold War history.

title: 'Blockbuster' history of Alexander the Great wins £50,000 Baillie Gifford prize
extract: Edmund Richardson's Alexander: God, King, Man has become the first ancient-history title to win the Baillie Gifford nonfiction prize, drawing on new archaeology and decoded Babylonian records.

title: Winner of the Prix Goncourt literary prize admits to using AI
extract: Prix Goncourt winner Philippe Jaenada says he used ChatGPT three times while writing his novel, including to plant a sentence and generate absurd answers for a technical detail.

title: Was one of the great novels of the Enlightenment written by a man who thought he was a werewolf?
extract: A new Swiss exhibition revisits Jan Potocki's surreal 18th-century novel The Manuscript Found in Saragossa, exploring its strange origins and the author's fascination with the supernatural.

title: American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee review - a gloriously immersive follow-up to Pachinko
extract: Min Jin Lee's follow-up to Pachinko traces a Korean family across Seoul, Sydney and California over three decades, using the pressures of private tutoring to examine migration, class and ambition.

title: Where to start with: John Berger
extract: On the centenary of John Berger's birth, the Guardian offers a route through his fiction, essays and art criticism, from G. and To the Wedding to Ways of Seeing.

title: Black Doves review - Ben Whishaw, Keira Knightley and Sarah Lancashire are spine-tinglingly good
extract: The second season of the British espionage drama returns with Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw and Sarah Lancashire; the Guardian praises its performances and emotional core despite its implausible plotting.

title: Adam Driver confirms Star Wars Kylo Ren film he worked on with Steven Soderbergh is dead: 'Yeah, it's over'
extract: Adam Driver says the standalone Ben Solo/Kylo Ren film he developed with Steven Soderbergh and a completed writing team is no longer happening after Lucasfilm declined the project.

title: Grimes is going to star in an AI movie that's coming to theaters
extract: Grimes will lend her likeness and voice to Gods Don't Give Gifts, an AI-generated science-fiction anthology due in theatres on December 4, testing whether AI filmmaking can support a commercial release.

title: 'George Lucas told me off for wearing lipstick': Celia Imrie on Traitors, Star Wars and treating the lens like a lover
extract: Celia Imrie recalls being cast as Bravo 5 in The Phantom Menace, being reprimanded by George Lucas for lipstick, and her time in The Traitors and Absolutely Fabulous.

title: TV tonight: the final episode of gloriously daft sketch show Ellie & Natasia
extract: The Guardian highlights the final episode of Ellie White and Natasia Demetriou's sketch comedy, praising its short run and absurd modern-manners humour.

title: Dave Grohl started 'sobbing like a baby' after performing with AC/DC
extract: Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl describes breaking down backstage after joining AC/DC for Highway to Hell at MetLife Stadium, calling the experience a full-circle moment rooted in his childhood love of the band.
